title: SLO Reliability Economics Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes how we design, negotiate, and operationalize SLOs with explicit cost/capacity tradeoffs. It codifies the decision flow from product SLA asks to SRE capacity commitments, the error‑budget response ladder, and post‑incident economic reconciliation.

Scope: Applies to all customer‑facing inference services (hosted inference API, dedicated pools, private connectors) and their supporting infra (routing, cache, autoscaler). Excludes non‑production experiments unless they are part of an admission review.

Audience: SREs, Product Managers, Platform Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success leads.

Definitions
- SLO: Service Level Objective expressed as a measurable target (e.g., p95 latency < 250ms).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO. Tracked as burn rate over rolling windows.
- Economic capacity: expected cost ($/qps or $/token) to deliver at SLO.
- Admission: formal gating that converts a product feature into capacity and SLO commitments.

Principles
- Make tradeoffs explicit: Every SLO must include an economic estimate and capacity owner.
- Measure at token/request granularity: per-route telemetry and cost attribution is required.
- Automate guardrails: automated throttles and canary rollbacks for rapid enforcement.
- Blameless, evidence-first reviews anchored to SLO burn and economic impact.

1) SLO design template (recommended fields)
- service_name: human-friendly identifier
- objective: metric and target (e.g., request_success_rate >= 99.5% over 30d)
- window: rolling window for target evaluation (30d / 7d / 24h)
- measurement_source: primary (prometheus/exporter) and secondary (trace sampling)
- alerting_quantile: which quantiles trigger alerts (p50/p95/p99)
- error_budget_quota: allowed budget (e.g., 0.5% of requests per 30d)
- economic_estimate: expected $/1000 requests and $/token with assumptions
- owner: team + oncall rotation contact
- admission_ticket: internal JIRA/Req ID

Example SLO (text block to copy into onboarding ticket)
service_name: inference-api-v2
objective: p95_latency_ms < 250ms
window: 30d
measurement_source: metrics/redwood/inference/p95_latency_ms
error_budget_quota: 0.5% over 30d
economic_estimate: $0.45 / 1k requests (avg seq_len=64, GPU-v100 equivalent)
owner: inference-runtime-team

2) Error budget policy and response ladder
The policy maps burn thresholds to required actions. All thresholds use a 1h and 24h burn view.
- Green: burn_rate <= 1x (no action). Continue standard monitoring.
- Amber I: 1x < burn_rate <= 5x (oncall aware). Actions: open incident note, reduce non‑critical background jobs, evaluate prefix cache hit improvement.
- Amber II: 5x < burn_rate <= 15x (oncall and pagination). Actions: initiate temporary throttles on non‑critical tenants, enable burst capacity (if available), escalate to SRE lead and product PM.
- Red: burn_rate > 15x or reserve exhausted. Actions: execute emergency capacity cut (see Runbook section), route traffic to fallback model variant, engage customer success, schedule mandatory postmortem within 48h.

Notes:
- Burn rate calculation: observed_error_budget_consumed / expected_per_window, where expected uses the SLO window.
- Thresholds are adjustable per service tier (enterprise customers may have stricter internal thresholds).

3) Capacity negotiation and admission process (stepwise)
1. Product files admission ticket with: feature description, expected qps, expected seq_len distribution, SLO proposal using the template above, and desired launch date.
2. SRE run a quick capacity delta analysis using historical analogs and estimated kernel/throughput numbers. Deliverable: a Capacity Delta Card (CSV) with columns: region, qps_peak, qps_95, estimated_gpu_hours/day, incremental_cost_estimate.
3. Alignment meeting (15–30m): participants: product PM, SRE owner, infra cost owner, solutions engineer. Decide on: required reserved capacity, soft throttles, rollout canary size, and whether to require a dedicated pool. Capture decision and signoff on the admission_ticket.
4. Implementation: routing rules, quota allocations, dashboard slices, and autoscaler tuning committed before launch.
5. Launch monitoring: 72h elevated monitoring window with oncall escalation matrix.

Capacity Delta Card (text table example)
region | peak_qps | qps_95 | est_gpu_hours/day | est_cost/day
us-east-1 | 450 | 320 | 18 | $1,350
eu-west-1 | 120 | 90 | 5 | $380

4) Automated guardrails and throttles
- Priority lanes: token_priority and request_priority tags. High priority (api_key enterprise) bypasses some soft throttles.
- Autoscaler knobs: target_cpu_utilization 70%, target_gpu_mem_util 75%, max_replicas based on cost cap. Example snippet to apply: 

kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-runtime-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference-runtime
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 40
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: gpu_utilization
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 75
EOF

- Cost cap enforcement: when projected incremental cost > daily budget percent, trigger routing to model-compact variant and throttle non‑latency‑sensitive features.

5) Runbook: emergency capacity reduction (Rogue burn > 15x)
Goal: stop burn within 15 minutes and re‑establish a safe headroom.
Owner: oncall responder + inference runtime engineer.
Actions (ordered):
1) Verify telemetry: confirm error budget burn via metrics dashboard and burn_rate panel.
2) If burn due to increased latency: run the following sequence in 1–2 minute windows:
  a. Enable model fallback: curl -X POST https://ops-api/redwood/route-switch -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","variant":"compact"}'
  b. Reduce per-tenant qps: set temporary soft quota via admin CLI: redwood-admin tenant-quota set --tenant-id <id> --qps <new-qps>
  c. If cacheable prefix patterns exist: flush and then prewarm cache using prewarm_job for top 10 prefixes.
3) If burn due to backend error spikes (5xx): scale up read replicas for the failing datastore if safe, or fail open to a degraded but healthy path for non‑critical features (see degradation matrix).
4) If capacity shortfall: trigger emergency reserved capacity (if committed) or gracefully shed lower priority tenants using token_priority tag.
5) Escalate: notify SRE lead and product PM. Open incident with severity classification.
6) Post mitigation: maintain elevated sampling (10% traces) for 24h and prepare evidence package for incident review.

6) Observability & dashboards (required views)
- SLO Overview dashboard: service list, current window SLO %, remaining error budget %, burn rate (1h, 24h), economic_cost_estimate.
- Latency quantiles by route: p50/p90/p95/p99 per route, colored by recently changed routes.
- Cost by route/tenant: $/hr and $/token, cumulative daily cost.
- Capacity headroom map: per-cluster free GPU slots, scheduled maintenance, and canary allocations.
- Incident evidence panel: linked traces, top offending tokens, and time‑sliced error budget consumption.

Instrumentation requirements (minimum)
- Metrics: request_count, success_count, latency_histogram (bucketed), model_variant, tenant_id, region, sequence_length.
- Traces: sample 2% baseline, increase to 10% during incidents or canaries.
- Logs: structured JSON with fields: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, input_token_count, latency_ms, error_code.

7) Incident review standards and evidence checklist
All SRE postmortems must include the following sections and artifacts:
- Summary: what happened, customer impact, duration, severity.
- Timeline: event timestamps with author/actor for each action.
- Evidence bundle: metric snapshots (SLO window before/during/after), trace links (10 representative traces), capacity delta card, and change history (deploys/config changes).
- Root cause analysis: causal chain and contributing factors.
- Corrective actions: short, medium, long-term with owners and target dates.
- Economic reconciliation: incremental cost during incident, estimated lost revenue or credit exposure if applicable.
- Learning: at least one measurable guardrail change (alert threshold, autoscaler rule, or route rule).

Postmortem timeline rules
- Draft within 72 hours, review within 7 days, final owner signoff within 21 days.
- If incident affected SLAs for paying customers, Customer Success must be looped in before the 72h draft.

8) Operational tooling recommendations
- Evidence collector (internal CLI): redwood-sre-collect --service inference-api-v2 --since 2026-02-03T12:00Z --out incident-20260203.tar.gz (collects dashboards, traces, logs, deploy history).
- Burn rate simulator: a small tool to run hypothetical traffic mixes for negotiation (inputs: qps, seq_len distribution, model_variant weights). Always run before admission signoff.
- Capacity cost workbook: shared spreadsheet template with standard GPU unit costs, preemptible assumptions, and amortized networking charges. Use this for negotiation cards.

9) Ownership matrix
- SRE owner: maintains SLO metric, dashboards, and oncall support (inference-runtime-team).
- Product PM: defines business SLA and prioritizes features vs cost tradeoffs.
- Infra cost owner: certifies economic_estimate and approves reserved capacity purchases.
- Solutions Engineer: customer-specific capacity adjustments and onboarding.

10) Appendix: sample alert rules
- Alert A: SLO_degradation_warning
  - Expression: slo_remaining_percent < 80% AND slo_burn_rate_1h > 2
  - Severity: P3 (pager to SRE rotation)
- Alert B: SLO_emergency
  - Expression: slo_remaining_percent < 20% AND slo_burn_rate_1h > 10
  - Severity: P1 (page SRE lead + product PM)

11) Templates and artifacts
- Capacity Delta CSV template (attach as part of admission_ticket)
- SLO onboarding checklist (checkbox style): metrics wired, dashboard copied, alerts configured, emergency runbook validated, capacity card uploaded.
- Postmortem checklist: evidence bundle attached, action owners assigned, retrospective scheduled.

Related pages and references
- Link to admission policy, SLO naming standards, and cost spreadsheet (see related_pages).

Ownership and maintenance
- This document is maintained by the inference-runtime SRE guild. Annual review required or sooner if capacity billing model changes.

Feedback and improvements
- Proposed changes should be submitted as PRs to the SRE playbook repo and reviewed by at least two reviewers listed in this document.

End of document
